newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude, products futures end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude, products futures end sharply lower.

text.p: NYMEX crude and oil product futures ended sharply lower Wednesday after a bearish American Petroleum Institute report and resumed Iraqi crude exports.
January crude futures settled $1.04 a barrel lower at $23.38, having hit a low of $23.15 during the session.
"A lot of the length in the market has been liquidated and there could still be more to go," said Andrew Lebow, a trader at commodity house ED&F Man.
"There were a couple of fundamental factors behind it, one obviously being the Iraqi deal finally going through," Lebow added.

Iraq's oil began to flow again in earnest on Wednesday, with reportedly 350,000 barrels a day going through the pipeline to the Turkish port of Ceyhan. Turkish state oil concer TUPRAS has had a deal approved by the U.N. to lift 75,000 bpd and both Coastal and Texaco said Wednesday that they are among those close to finalizing deals.
"Last week there was a little bit of skepticism over whether (the "oil-for-food" deal) was going to get done or go to the brink and Saddam maybe would do something to K.O. the deal," said Lebow.
"Now, reality has hit and that is one of fundamental catalysts," he said.
Analysts also say the API report late Tuesday and Wednesday's Energy Information Agency's figures confirmed the recent cash market indications that the product markets were weakening.

The API showed a very sharp rise of nearly six million barrels in gasoline stocks last week. Distillates -- heating oil, diesel -- also continued to recover to more seasonal levels, while crude stocks rose sharply in the key Gulf refining area.

January gasoline hit a low of 62.80 cents a gallon on Wednesday before recovering to settle at 63.56, down 3.3 cents. January heating oil sunk to 66.40 cents a gallon before ending down 2.8 cents at 66.82 cents.
